method: Fifty new natural-language questions created for a paired Ask AI 1 and Ask AI 2 full-text relevance evaluation. Anchor topics document coverage only and are not supplied to either retrieval method.

questions.question: Why does the Genesis flood story contain details that appear to come from two different versions?
Why does Deuteronomy describe some laws and events differently from Exodus and Numbers?
Why do scholars date the book of Daniel to the time of Antiochus Epiphanes rather than the Babylonian exile?
How does 1 Enoch explain the origin of demons and evil through the story of the Watchers?
How did early Christians reinterpret passages from the Hebrew Bible as predictions about Jesus?
Did Isaiah 7 originally predict that a virgin would give birth to the Messiah?
Why was the Greek Septuagint so important for New Testament authors and early Christians?
What are the books of the Maccabees, and why are they absent from many Protestant Bibles?
What did ancient Jewish apocalyptic writers expect God to do at the end of the present age?
How did Pharisees and Sadducees differ over resurrection, angels, and the authority of oral tradition?
Did Jesus expect the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple within his own generation?
What did Jesus mean by the kingdom of God, and did he think it was already present or still future?
Was Jesus' command to love enemies intended as a practical ethic for ordinary life?
How can historians evaluate claims that Jesus performed miracles without deciding whether miracles are possible?
What do Jesus' exorcisms reveal about ancient beliefs concerning demons and illness?
How do Matthew and Luke tell different versions of Jesus' temptation in the wilderness?
Why do the genealogies of Jesus in Matthew and Luke disagree about his ancestors?
Is there historical evidence that Herod ordered the massacre of infants in Bethlehem?
What point was Jesus making with the parable of the Good Samaritan?

questions.anchorTopic: Signs in the Gospel of John
questions.question: Why does John call Jesus' miracles signs, and what are they meant to reveal about him?
What role did Mary Magdalene play among Jesus' followers and in the earliest resurrection traditions?
Why did Judas betray Jesus, and do the Gospels agree about his motives and death?
Why do the Gospels portray Pontius Pilate as reluctant to execute Jesus when other sources describe him as brutal?
How historically plausible is the claim that Joseph of Arimathea placed Jesus in a known tomb?
Is an empty tomb necessary to explain why Jesus' followers came to believe he had been raised?
How do the accounts of Paul's conversion in Acts differ from Paul's own description in Galatians?
What did Paul mean by justification through faith in his letter to the Romans?
Why were some Christians in Corinth denying a future resurrection of the dead?
Does the Christ poem in Philippians teach that Jesus existed in heaven before his human life?
What vocabulary and theology lead many scholars to question whether Paul wrote Colossians?
How do restrictions on women in the Pastoral Epistles differ from women's roles in Paul's undisputed letters?
Do Paul's speeches in Acts accurately represent the theology found in his letters?
Does the Letter of James contradict Paul's teaching that people are justified by faith rather than works?
Were Peter and Cephas the same apostle, and why have some scholars argued that they were different people?
Did Paul expect Jesus to return before Paul and most of his converts died?
Did the Gospel of Mark originally end with the women fleeing the empty tomb in fear?
How did the passage known as the Johannine Comma become part of later copies of 1 John?
Why do scholars conclude that the story of the woman caught in adultery was not originally in John's Gospel?
Was Luke's account of Jesus sweating blood added by a later scribe, and why would someone add it?
Did Christian scribes alter passages that could be used to support adoptionist views of Jesus?
How is the kingdom of God presented in the sayings of the Gospel of Thomas?
Does the Gospel of Judas portray Judas as Jesus' favored disciple or as a condemned figure?
What was discovered at Nag Hammadi, and how did it change the study of early Christianity?
How did Constantine's conversion change the legal and political position of Christianity in the Roman Empire?
What disagreement about Christ led to the conflict between Arius and his opponents at the Council of Nicaea?
How did Augustine develop the doctrine of original sin from his reading of Paul?
Did Origen teach that all rational beings, including the devil, would eventually be saved?
Why can studying contradictions and manuscript differences create problems for belief in biblical inerrancy?
How does Bart prepare for public debates with evangelical or conservative Christian scholars?
How does Bart's blog use membership fees and fundraising campaigns to support charitable causes?
